resources.string: Jetpack Compose is Android’s modern toolkit for native UI development. It simplifies and accelerates UI development on Android.
Composable functions are the building blocks of Compose. They let you define your UI hierarchy programmatically.
Use Row to place elements horizontally and Column to place them vertically. They are fundamental layout building blocks.
Modifiers allow you to decorate or augment a composable. You can change size, padding, background, or add click actions.
State represents value that can change over time. Using remember and mutableStateOf triggers UI recomposition automatically.
LazyColumn is used to display vertically scrolling lists of items efficiently by only rendering visible items on screen.
Material 3 provides dynamic coloring, typography, and shapes to give your app a cohesive and modern look and feel.
Display images using the Image composable and control how they scale inside their bounds using ContentScale.
Cards are surfaces that display content and actions on a single topic, providing elevation and rounded corners.
Scaffold provides a structure for your app\'s screen, managing slots for TopAppBar, BottomBar, and floating action buttons.
Bring your UI to life with smooth transitions, animateContentSize, and state-based animations in Compose.
Handle user interactions easily using Button, IconButton, or by adding a clickable modifier to any surface.
Customize text size, color, weights, and font families using MaterialTheme typography styles.
Control spatial distribution using padding modifiers and Spacer composables to avoid cluttered layouts.
Fine-tune child alignment inside rows and columns using Arrangement and Alignment parameters.
Load strings via stringResource(), images via painterResource(), and dimensions to support multiple screens.
Use Layout Inspector in Android Studio to inspect your Composable hierarchy and track recompositions.
Ensure your app is usable by everyone by providing meaningful content descriptions and proper touch target sizes.
Write unit tests for your ViewModels and business logic to ensure code reliability and prevent regressions.
Use Compose Testing library to test your UI components, simulate clicks, and verify screen states.
Navigate smoothly between multiple screens using the Jetpack Navigation component tailored for Compose.
Separate UI state from business logic by holding screen state safely inside ViewModels.
Handle asynchronous data streams reactively using Kotlin Flows and Coroutines inside your Android apps.
Persist structured data locally on device storage securely using SQLite-based Room libraries.
Fetch data from web APIs and JSON endpoints effortlessly using Retrofit and Moshi or Gson converters.
Manage dependencies cleanly and testably across your app architecture using Hilt and Dagger.
Execute background tasks reliably even if the app closes or the device restarts using WorkManager.
Leverage floating action buttons, snackbars, and bottom sheets out-of-the-box with Material 3.
Avoid unnecessary recompositions, stabilize parameters, and optimize your Lazy lists for smooth 60fps performance.
Prepare your signed App Bundle (AAB), set up store listings, and publish your finished app to the Google Play Store.
